description: We are interested in space exploration, astronomy, scientific discovery, problem-solving, and using technology to turn creative ideas into meaningful solutions. We believe that curiosity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn can make a big difference—even when we are exploring something new.
summary: THE LAST SIGNAL is an interactive digital museum that preserves and shares the stories of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It brings mission histories, equipment information, scientific contributions, and known mission outcomes into one accessible, space-themed learning experience. Visitors can explore the Moon Archives and Mars Archives, read Mission Stories, follow an Interactive Timeline, and use Then & Now to understand the historical context and legacy of selected equipment. The Last Words presents fictional first-person narratives inspired by documented mission histories; these are creative interpretations, not actual NASA transmissions. A 10-question Space Quiz provides immediate feedback and explanations, while Space Legacy highlights the scientific and historical value of exploration hardware. By turning overlooked mission equipment into engaging stories, the project makes the history of planetary exploration more accessible and memorable.
details: THE LAST SIGNAL is a browser-based digital museum developed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge topic of storytelling about discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. The website presents information about selected space exploration equipment and missions through dedicated Moon Archives and Mars Archives. Visitors can explore Mission Stories containing mission backgrounds, objectives, achievements, equipment information, and known mission outcomes. The Interactive Timeline presents important events chronologically, while Then & Now helps visitors understand the historical context and continuing significance of the equipment. One of the distinctive features is The Last Words, which presents fictional first-person narratives inspired by documented mission histories. These are creative interpretations and do not represent actual NASA transmissions or recordings. The website also includes a Space Quiz with 10 multiple-choice questions, immediate feedback, and explanations, along with Space Legacy, which highlights the scientific and historical contributions of space exploration. The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. Google Antigravity was used as an AI-assisted development tool to support website development. The website was deployed using Render. Its dark cosmic visual theme, space-related backgrounds, responsive navigation, animated elements, and interactive sections create an engaging learning experience. The project aims to make the stories and contributions of overlooked space equipment more accessible, understandable, and interesting to students and the wider public.
